title: Degreewise surjective module-complex towers compute their derived limit termwise
statement: Let $(A_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse system of commutative rings with limit $A=\varprojlim_n A_n$. Let $P_n^\bullet$ be cochain complexes of $A_n$-modules with $A_{n+1}$-linear chain maps $t_n:P_{n+1}^\bullet\to P_n^\bullet$, the target being restricted along $A_{n+1}\to A_n$. Assume every $t_n^i:P_{n+1}^i\to P_n^i$ is surjective. Define the complex $P^\bullet$ of $A$-modules by $P^i=\varprojlim_nP_n^i$ with componentwise differentials. Then the images of the projections $P^\bullet\to P_n^\bullet$ exhibit $Q(P^\bullet)$ as a derived limit of $(Q(P_n^\bullet),Q(t_n))$ in $D(A)$ [def-weil-derived-limit, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], all $P_n^\bullet$ here restricted to $A$; explicitly they form the first arrow of a distinguished Roos triangle $Q(P^\bullet)\to\prod_nQ(P_n^\bullet)\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nQ(P_n^\bullet)\to Q(P^\bullet)[1]$. The identification respects the projection maps. Inverse systems are as in [def-weil-inverse-system].

source.place: Tag 091D, lemma-compute-Rlim-modules, clauses (3) and (5); Tag 0CQD, lemma-distinguished-triangle-Rlim-modules

proof.text: Restrict each $P_n^\bullet$ along the projection $A\to A_n$. If $a=(a_m)_m\in A$, then $t_n(a_{n+1}x)=a_n t_n(x)$ by the given $A_{n+1}$-linearity and compatibility of $a$. Thus all transitions are $A$-linear. Put $B^i=\prod_{n\geq1}P_n^i$, $d_B((x_n))=(d_nx_n)$, $j^i:P^i\to B^i$ the inclusion of compatible tuples, and $u^i((x_n))=(x_n-t_n(x_{n+1}))$. The equations $d_n t_n=t_n d_{n+1}$ imply $d_Bu=ud_B$ and $d_Bj=jd_P$; componentwise $d_B^2=d_P^2=0$. These give complexes and chain maps $P^\bullet\xrightarrow{j}B^\bullet\xrightarrow{u}B^\bullet$ in the sense of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0CQD, lemma-distinguished-triangle-Rlim-modules, proof via lemma-distinguished-triangle-Rlim, first paragraph; Tag 091D, lemma-compute-Rlim-modules

proof.text: For each integer $i$, $\ker u^i$ consists exactly of tuples satisfying $x_n=t_n(x_{n+1})$, hence equals $j^i(P^i)$ and $j^i$ is injective. Given $y=(y_n)\in B^i$, set $x_1=0$ and recursively choose $x_{n+1}$ with $t_n^i(x_{n+1})=x_n-y_n$; this is possible by surjectivity. Then $u^i(x)=y$. The choices need not be linear or commute with differentials: they prove only surjectivity of $u^i$. Consequently $0\to P^\bullet\xrightarrow{j}B^\bullet\xrightarrow{u}B^\bullet\to0$ is a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes. This is the short exact sequence used in the first paragraph of the proof of Stacks Tag 0CQD, with its surjectivity here proved directly.

source.place: Tag 0CQD, lemma-distinguished-triangle-Rlim-modules, proof via lemma-distinguished-triangle-Rlim, first paragraph; Tag 091D, lemma-compute-Rlim-modules

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso] to the short exact sequence in step 2. It gives a quasi-isomorphism $q:C(j)\to B^\bullet$, equal to $u$ on the unshifted $B^\bullet$ summand and zero on the shifted $P^\bullet$ summand. If $i:B^\bullet\to C(j)$ is the cone inclusion, then $qi=u$. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $Q(q)$ is invertible and the cone triangle $Q(P^\bullet)\xrightarrow{Q(j)}Q(B^\bullet)\xrightarrow{Q(i)}Q(C(j))\xrightarrow{-Q(p)}Q(P^\bullet)[1]$ is distinguished. Set $\delta=-Q(p)Q(q)^{-1}$. The triple $(\mathrm{id}_{Q(P)},\mathrm{id}_{Q(B)},Q(q))$ is an isomorphism of triangles: its first square is the identity, its second square is $Q(q)Q(i)=Q(u)$, and its last square is $\delta Q(q)=-Q(p)$. All three components are invertible. Hence the isomorphism-closure axiom in [def-weil-triangulated-category] applies. This gives the distinguished triangle $Q(P^\bullet)\xrightarrow{Q(j)}Q(B^\bullet)\xrightarrow{Q(u)}Q(B^\bullet)\xrightarrow{-Q(p)Q(q)^{-1}}Q(P^\bullet)[1]$, with the first two arrows unchanged.

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor, formula for the connecting morphism and preceding cone comparison

proof.text: The category of $A$-modules has exact countable products: for any family of short exact sequences the product kernel is the product of the kernels (checked componentwise), and a tuple in the product of the quotients has a tuple of preimages by choosing a preimage in each factor. Products and the zero object carry the componentwise module structures. Apply [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core] to this abelian module category and the countable family of complexes $P_n^\bullet$. Its assertion that the image under $Q$ of every termwise product cone is limiting identifies $Q(B^\bullet)$, with the maps $Q(\mathrm{pr}_n)$, as $\prod_n Q(P_n^\bullet)$ in $D(A)$. No boundedness, finite generation, or surjectivity of the ring transitions is needed.

source.place: Tag 07KC, lemma-products, clauses (1) and (2); referenced immediately before Tag 0CQD in more-algebra.tex

proof.text: The equality $\mathrm{pr}_n u=\mathrm{pr}_n-t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$ of chain maps remains true under the additive localization $Q$. Under the product identification of step 4, $Q(u)$ is therefore precisely the morphism $1-s$ specified in [def-weil-derived-limit]. Moreover $Q(\mathrm{pr}_n)Q(j)=Q(p_n)$, where $p_n:P^\bullet\to P_n^\bullet$ is the original projection. Thus the distinguished triangle of step 3 is the asserted Roos triangle, with the specified projections, and the definition [def-weil-derived-limit] proves the claim.
